source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Group O red blood cells lack A and B antigens and can be used for recipients of other ABO groups when emergency red-cell transfusion is required before typing is known.","B":"Group O red blood cells are universal recipients and can receive red cells from every ABO group.","C":"Group O red blood cells express both A and B antigens, which makes them compatible with all recipients.","D":"AB plasma and group O red cells use the same ABO compatibility rule because plasma and red-cell compatibility are interchangeable."}}
source_row.rationale: AABB identifies type O red blood cells as emergency red-cell units that can be given when the recipient’s ABO type is not yet known. The final item is deliberately limited to ABO red-cell compatibility and does not overgeneralize Rh selection or plasma compatibility.
source_row.source_detail: ABO red-cell compatibility: in an emergency, type O red blood cells can be given when the recipient blood type is not yet known.
